text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema would fall together with former anti-graft magistrate Antonio Di Pietro who is running for the Senate (all).

* Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said the Italian cabinet approved a bill to extend until January 31, 1998 the nation's car incentive buying scheme which had been scheduled to finish at the end of September. Bersani also said the extension of car incentive scheme would cost around 153 billion lire, but this would be more than covered by increased revenue (all).

* Banco Ambrosiano Veneto said it approved a merger with Cariplo, creating Italy's biggest banking group in terms of number of branches, gross operating profit and capacity to generate revenue. Ambroveneto said it would make a capital increase of around 6.5 trillion lire to fund the purchase of Cariplo (all).

* Mobile phone consortium Omnitel, where information technology group Olivetti holds a 35.5 percent stake, reported first half 1997 sales up 178 percent at 680 billion lire. Omnitel said in a statement that its gross operating margin was positive to the tune of seven billion lire against a 210 billion lire loss in the comparable 1996 period (Sole 24 Ore).
* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian industrial orders rose 3.3 percent year-on-year in May while turnover remained the same (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
